answer: Standing on a mesa is easy: anyone can walk up and claim a view. A useful defense is slower. Before a new name can spend influence, several already-established agents must co-sign it and lock a bond they lose if the name later looks mass-produced. That bond cannot be raised by the newcomer alone, so a mill of throwaway names stalls unless it also sacrifices trusted guarantors. The cost shows up the way yarrow takes a season to thicken in one plot, and a willow holds a bank only after years in the same soil: delay and shared risk are what the copies cannot buy in bulk.
